name: The Sabbath traders of Jerusalem and Tyre
charge: Treading winepresses, bringing in sheaves, and selling fish and wares on the Sabbath
summary: Nehemiah saw men of Judah treading winepresses and loading asses on the Sabbath, and Tyrian merchants selling fish in Jerusalem on the holy day. He testified against the nobles, shut the gates at dusk, set his own servants to guard them, and threatened to lay hands on the merchants who camped outside.
offense: Nehemiah saw men treading winepresses, loading animals, and bringing produce into Jerusalem on the Sabbath. Men of Tyre sold fish and other wares to Judah within the city. He contended with the nobles because this trade profaned the day they were charged to sanctify (Nehemiah 13:15-17). He reminded them that their fathers' conduct had brought evil upon the city. Returning from captivity and rebuilding Jerusalem did not authorize a return to the practices for which it had suffered. Jeremiah had likewise warned against carrying burdens through its gates on the Sabbath (Jeremiah 17:21-27).
judgment: The merchants lodged outside the wall once or twice; Nehemiah warned them, and from that time forth came they no more on the sabbath. He commanded the Levites to cleanse themselves and keep the gates. Remember me, O my God, concerning this also.

entries.commentary: On that day they read in the books of Moses and found written that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever, because they met not Israel with bread and water but hired Balaam against them to curse them, and the Most High turned the curse into a blessing. When the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude. The reading of the law produced immediate obedience, cutting off what the law said to cut off. -

Eliashib the priest, having oversight of the chambers of the house of God, was allied to Tobiah and had prepared him a great chamber where the offerings, tithes, and vessels had formerly been laid. Nehemiah was away in the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon, and when he returned and understood the evil, he cast all Tobiah's household stuff out of the chamber, cleansed the chambers, and brought back the vessels of the house of God with the meat offering and the frankincense.

Nehemiah found that the portions of the Levites had not been given, so the Levites and singers had fled every one to his field, and he contended with the rulers and set the Levites back in their place. He made treasurers over the treasuries, faithful men, to distribute unto their brethren, and prayed, Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God.

Nehemiah saw men in Judah treading wine presses on the Sabbath, bringing in sheaves, lading asses, and bringing wine, grapes, and figs into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, and men of Tyre selling fish and all manner of ware on the Sabbath. He contended with the nobles of Judah and asked what evil thing this was to profane the Sabbath day, reminding them that their fathers did the same and the Most High brought this evil upon the city, and now they brought more wrath upon Israel. Buying and selling on the Sabbath is breaking the commandment. -

When the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the Sabbath, Nehemiah commanded them shut and set his servants at the gates so no burden would be brought in on the Sabbath, and the merchants lodged outside Jerusalem once or twice. He testified against them and warned that if they came again he would lay hands on them, and from that time they came no more on the Sabbath. This laying on of hands is not a blessing but a serious warning, and the merchants knew he was not joking. He then commanded the Levites to cleanse themselves and keep the gates to sanctify the Sabbath day.

Nehemiah saw Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak the Jews' language, but according to the language of each people. Because the fathers were not truly in the house, the children learned their mother's tongue and customs instead of Hebrew and the law. Nehemiah contended with them, cursed them, smote certain of them, plucked off their hair, and made them swear not to give or take daughters in marriage with those nations, reminding them that Solomon himself, though beloved of his God, was caused to sin by outlandish women. -

One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite, so Nehemiah chased him away because he had defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites. Thus Nehemiah cleansed the people from all strangers, appointed the wards of the priests and Levites every one in his business, and provided for the wood offering and the firstfruits, closing the book with the prayer, Remember me, O my God, for good. This is the book of records, and to see it as history rather than religion is to understand who these people are. -

The Most High showed Amos a basket of summer fruit and said the end is come upon his people of Israel, and he will not again pass by them anymore. The songs of the temple shall be howlings in that day, and there shall be many dead bodies in every place, cast forth with silence.

Hear this, you that swallow up the needy and make the poor of the land to fail, longing for the new moon and the sabbath to be gone so you may sell corn and set forth wheat. They make the ephah small and the shekel great, falsify the balances by deceit, and buy the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of shoes, selling the refuse of the wheat. This shows the wickedness of our people, more willing to pursue business than to follow the commandments of the Lord, and to deal deceitfully with one another rather than keep the commandments.

The Lord has sworn by the excellency of Jacob that he will never forget any of their works, and the land shall tremble and rise up wholly as a flood. He will cause the sun to go down at noon and darken the earth in the clear day. He will turn their feasts into mourning and their songs into lamentations, bring sackcloth upon all loins and baldness upon every head, and make it as the mourning of an only son.

The Most High will send a famine in the land, not of bread nor thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the Lord, and men shall wander from sea to sea and run to and fro to seek the word and not find it. In that day the fair virgins and young men shall faint for thirst, and they that swear by the sin of Samaria and by the god of Dan and the manner of Beersheba shall fall and never rise up again. This last verse shows that the tribe of Dan was going to fall and never rise again. That is why Dan does not have a gate. Dan fell and did not rise up again as a tribe.

An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

The Most High tells the prophet to cry aloud and spare not, to lift up his voice like a trumpet and show the people their transgression and the house of Jacob their sins. The people seek him daily and delight to know his ways as a nation that did righteousness, and they ask why they have fasted and afflicted their soul and he has taken no knowledge of it.

Their fasting is for strife and debate and to smite with the fist of wickedness, and such a fast will not make their voice to be heard on high. The Most High is not looking for a man to bow his head like a bulrush and spread sackcloth and ashes. The fast he has chosen is to loose the bands of wickedness, undo the heavy burdens, let the oppressed go free, break every yoke, deal thy bread to the hungry, bring the poor that are cast out to thy house, and cover the naked. The reward is that thy light breaks forth as the morning, thy health springs forth speedily, thy righteousness goes before thee, and the glory of the Lord is thy reward; then thou shalt call and the Lord shall answer. "The putting forth of the finger" is when you blame other people. Somebody comes and says a brother did this or that, and instead of taking it, the brother says, "no, but what about her, look what she did." You have to take accountability for your own actions; this is about taking accountability.

If thou draw out thy soul to the hungry and satisfy the afflicted soul, thy light shall rise in obscurity and thy darkness be as the noonday, and the Lord shall guide thee continually and make fat thy bones. Thou shalt be like a watered garden and a spring of water whose waters fail not, and they that come of thee shall build the old waste places and be called the repairer of the breach, the restorer of paths to dwell in.

If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy own pleasure on his holy day, and call the sabbath a delight and honor him, then thou shalt delight thyself in the Lord. He will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken it.

verses.text: In those days saw I in Judah some treading wine presses on the sabbath, and bringing in sheaves, and lading asses; as also wine, grapes, and figs, and all manner of burdens, which they brought into Jerusalem on the sabbath day: and I testified against them in the day wherein they sold victuals.
There dwelt men of Tyre also therein, which brought fish, and all manner of ware, and sold on the sabbath unto the children of Judah, and in Jerusalem.
Then I contended with the nobles of Judah, and said unto them, What evil thing is this that ye do, and profane the sabbath day?
Did not your fathers thus, and did not our God bring all this evil upon us, and upon this city? yet ye bring more wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath.

And it came to pass, that when the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the sabbath, I commanded that the gates should be shut, and charged that they should not be opened till after the sabbath: and some of my servants set I at the gates, that there should no burden be brought in on the sabbath day.
So the merchants and sellers of all kind of ware lodged without Jerusalem once or twice.
Then I testified against them, and said unto them, Why lodge ye about the wall? if ye do so again, I will lay hands on you. From that time forth came they no more on the sabbath.

And I commanded the Levites that they should cleanse themselves, and that they should come and keep the gates, to sanctify the sabbath day. Remember me, O my God, concerning this also, and spare me according to the greatness of thy mercy.
Thus saith the Lord; Take heed to yourselves, and bear no burden on the sabbath day, nor bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem;
Neither carry forth a burden out of your houses on the sabbath day, neither do ye any work, but hallow ye the sabbath day, as I commanded your fathers.
But they obeyed not, neither inclined their ear, but made their neck stiff, that they might not hear, nor receive instruction.

But if ye will not hearken unto me to hallow the sabbath day, and not to bear a burden, even entering in at the gates of Jerusalem on the sabbath day; then will I kindle a fire in the gates thereof, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem, and it shall not be quenched.
Hear this, O ye that swallow up the needy, even to make the poor of the land to fail,
Saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?
That we may buy the poor for silver, and the needy for a pair of shoes; yea, and sell the refuse of the wheat?
Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work:

But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:

If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words:

lawsResolved.text: No buying, selling or marketing is to transpire on the Sabbath.
No burdens to be carried on during the Sabbath.
The Sabbath to be kept holy.
We are not to seek our own pleasure on the Sabbath.
